_readme: Load-bearing figures for italian-estate.com. A figure phrase used in two or more articles is a corpus-wide claim and must be registered here with its source; a figure used once is a local worked example and needs no entry. Adding an entry is a claim about the world, so each needs a source and an asOf date, and the scorer reports every entry a change introduces so a reviewer sees them. Entries are grouped per figure, because one number can carry more than one meaning: 2% is the prima casa registration rate and also the Salva Casa tolerance for post-2024 works.
_scope: Italian figures only. A claim about Portuguese, Spanish, Greek, Maltese or Croatian tax belongs in external-claims.json, keyed by the claim rather than by the number, because nobody here monitors those jurisdictions and because their numbers collide with Italian ones.
_seeding: This registry starts from the figures verified against primary sources during the two new-article waves of August 2026, not from a sweep of what the corpus happens to repeat. Registering a figure the corpus repeats without checking it is how an unsourced number acquires the appearance of provenance, which is the failure this file exists to prevent. It is deliberately incomplete: the corpus carries 381 load-bearing figures and the rewrite waves populate the rest as each page is actually checked.

facts.statement: Cedolare secca rate on short-let income from the first residential unit a landlord lets in a tax year
facts.source: Legge di Bilancio 2024 (L. 213/2023) art. 1 co. 63; Agenzia delle Entrate guidance on locazioni brevi

facts.source: Legge di Bilancio 2024 (L. 213/2023) art. 1 co. 63

facts.source: Legge di Bilancio 2024 (L. 213/2023) art. 1 co. 64-67

facts.source: DPR 131/1986 Tariffa Parte I art. 1; prezzo-valore per L. 266/2005 art. 1 co. 497

facts.source: DPR 131/1986 Tariffa Parte I art. 1, nota II-bis

facts.statement: VAT on a new-build purchase in the luxury cadastral categories A/1, A/8 and A/9
facts.source: DPR 633/1972; cadastral categories per DM 2 agosto 1969

facts.source: Legge di Bilancio 2024 (L. 213/2023) art. 1 co. 91

facts.statement: IVAFE, the Italian tax an Italian resident pays on financial assets held abroad
facts.source: DL 201/2011 art. 19; Legge di Bilancio 2024 for the 0.4% rate on blacklisted jurisdictions

facts.statement: Interesse legale for 2026, used for late-payment interest and for ravvedimento operoso arithmetic
facts.source: DM Economia e Finanze 10 dicembre 2025

facts.statement: Floor rate applied to usufruct and bare-ownership valuation tables, which is why the 2026 tables did not move when the legal rate fell
facts.source: DPR 131/1986 art. 46 and the annual usufruct coefficient decree

facts.statement: IRES, the Italian corporate income tax rate applying to a company holding Italian property
facts.source: TUIR art. 77

facts.statement: Minimum floor area for a habitable single-occupant dwelling after the Salva Casa reform, reduced from 28 sqm
facts.source: DL 69/2024 conv. L. 105/2024 art. 1; DM Sanità 5 luglio 1975 as amended

facts.statement: Minimum floor area for a habitable dwelling for two occupants after the Salva Casa reform
facts.source: DL 69/2024 conv. L. 105/2024 art. 1; DM Sanità 5 luglio 1975 as amended

facts.statement: Share of Italian homes carrying catastrophe cover, against a mandatory regime that applies to firms only
facts.source: ANIA, Italian insurance association, cat-nat exposure data 2025

facts.statement: Comuni classified in seismic zone 1, the highest hazard band, where sismabonus and the strictest NTC rules apply
facts.source: Dipartimento della Protezione Civile, classificazione sismica dei comuni italiani

facts.statement: Minimum Sangiovese share in Chianti Classico DOCG
facts.source: Disciplinare di produzione dei vini DOP Chianti Classico art. 2

facts.statement: Maximum grape-to-wine conversion rate, Chianti Classico DOCG
facts.source: Disciplinare di produzione dei vini DOP Chianti Classico art. 4

Swiss withholding rate applied to new Italy-Switzerland cross-border workers, expressed as a share of ordinary cantonal rates, under the agreement of 23 December 2020
facts.source: Accordo Italia-Svizzera 23.12.2020, ratified by L. 83/2023, in force 17 July 2023

facts.statement: Italian exempt band on cross-border employment income for frontalieri
facts.source: L. 83/2023 and implementing Italian provisions on frontalieri taxation

facts.statement: Minimum duration of a concession on the Lombardy lake and waterway domain
facts.source: Regolamento regionale Lombardia 9/2015, disciplina della gestione del demanio lacuale e idroviario

facts.statement: Maximum duration of a concession on the Lombardy lake and waterway domain
facts.source: Regolamento regionale Lombardia 9/2015, disciplina della gestione del demanio lacuale e idroviario

facts.statement: Maximum duration of the substitute-tax regime for new Italian residents under art. 24-bis TUIR
facts.source: Art. 24-bis TUIR; increase to EUR 200,000 for residence transferred after 10 August 2024

facts.statement: Duration of the 7% substitute-tax regime for foreign pensioners under art. 24-ter TUIR
facts.source: Art. 24-ter TUIR; population ceiling raised from 20,000 to 30,000 from 7 April 2026

facts.statement: Statutory IMU base rate on residential property other than a primary residence, before any comune adjustment
facts.source: L. 160/2019 art. 1 c. 754 (Legge di Bilancio 2020), Gazzetta Ufficiale 19G00165; comune ceiling registered separately at 1.06%

facts.statement: Share of Italian residential transactions bought by foreign citizens in 2025, about 39,000 homes out of 766,756 normalised transactions
facts.source: Gate-away international buyers data for 2025 cross-referenced with OMI (Osservatorio del Mercato Immobiliare, Agenzia delle Entrate) transaction totals; verified against independent search results 2026-09-06

facts.statement: National average asking price per square metre for an Italian home, April 2026 reading, up 4.24% year on year. Asking price, not the notarised value OMI records.
facts.source: Immobiliare.it national asking-price index, April 2026 reading; registered in market-stats.json as italy_avg_price_sqm

facts.statement: Average asking price per square metre in the comune of Milan, April 2026. Distinct from the province at €4,148 and from Abitare Co metropolitan-area readings; district comparables are a further cut again.
facts.source: Immobiliare.it comune di Milano asking-price index, April 2026; cross-checked against a second index reading €5,481/sqm the same month

facts.statement: Growth in Italian residential transactions in 2025, to 766,757 normalised sales from 719,578 in 2024. The market expanded; earlier site copy asserted a contraction.
facts.source: Agenzia delle Entrate / OMI, Rapporto Immobiliare 2026 — Il settore residenziale, published 21 May 2026 with ABI

facts.statement: Lower bound of the all-in closing cost band this site publishes for a non-resident second home. An editorial composition decision on how to present a spread, not a measured market average.
facts.source: Owner decision recorded 2026-08-20 in market-stats.json (closing_cost_stack_non_resident), reconciling 7 competing bands across 125 pages

facts.statement: Upper bound of that same published closing cost band for a non-resident second home bought through an agency. Prima casa sits below it; a new-build with VAT can exceed it.
facts.source: Owner decision recorded 2026-08-20 in market-stats.json (closing_cost_stack_non_resident), reconciling 7 competing bands across 125 pages

facts.statement: Bonus ristrutturazioni deduction rate for 2026 where the renovated unit is the owner's main residence, spread over ten annual instalments within a 96,000 EUR cap per unit.
facts.source: Legge di Bilancio 2026 (L. 199/2025), confirming the bonus casa rates for the 2026 tax year

facts.statement: Bonus ristrutturazioni deduction rate for 2026 on second homes and other residential units, the rate that applies to a property bought to let.
facts.source: Legge di Bilancio 2026 (L. 199/2025); the rate falls to 30% on second homes from 2027

facts.statement: Statutory revaluation applied to the rendita catastale before the cadastral multiplier is used to reach cadastral value.
facts.source: L. 662/1996 art. 3 comma 48, the rivalutazione della rendita catastale still in force

facts.statement: Forfait deduction allowed against gross rental income under the progressive IRPEF regime, in place of itemised expenses.
facts.source: TUIR art. 37, the standard abbattimento forfettario on canone di locazione

facts.statement: Upper end of the loan-to-value Italian banks typically lend to a non-resident buyer, against materially higher ratios for residents. Market practice, not a statutory cap.
facts.source: Italian retail bank non-resident lending practice, tier B, cross-checked across lender product sheets 2026

facts.statement: Lower bound of the gap between cadastral value and market price on Italian residential stock, the reason IMU looks small against a purchase price. Rule of thumb, tier B.
facts.source: OMI cadastral versus market value comparisons; the gap commonly runs 30% to 50% and varies by comune

facts.statement: Deposit an Italian resident borrower is typically asked for, against 30% to 50% for a non-resident. Market practice rather than regulation.
facts.source: Italian retail mortgage market practice 2026, tier B, cross-checked across lender criteria

facts.statement: Upper band of professional property management fees as a share of rent, reached on short-let mandates where the manager handles turnover and compliance.
facts.source: Italian letting and STR management mandates, tier B, observed fee schedules across Milan, Rome, Florence and Puglia

facts.statement: Upper end of Italian estate agency commission charged to the buyer side before IVA, against a floor near 2% where a seller splits the fee.
facts.source: Italian agency mandate practice, tier B; FIAIP and regional usi e consuetudini put the common band at 2% to 6% plus IVA
